title: He asked for more.
paragraphs:
What if your prayers are small
not because God is limited—
but because your shame is?

What if you’ve been whispering
when God is inviting you to cry out?
We don’t talk about this enough.

The quiet guilt.
The hidden past.
The names people gave you… and the ones you gave yourself.

And slowly, without realizing it,
you shrink your prayers to match your pain.

You stop asking boldly
because you feel unworthy.

You stop expecting breakthrough
because you remember your mistakes.

You don’t say it out loud—
but deep inside, you believe:
“God will bless others… but not me.”
A man born under a curse.

“His mother named him Jabez, saying, ‘I gave birth to him in pain.’”
— 1 Chronicles 4:9

Every time his name was spoken—
it echoed his origin.
And yet… he refused to live inside it.
Jabez didn’t let his past silence his prayers.
He went straight to God—with boldness that almost feels uncomfortable.

“Oh, that You would bless me indeed, and enlarge my territory, that Your hand would be with me, and that You would keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!”
— 1 Chronicles 4:10
And here’s the line that should shake you:

“So God granted him what he requested.”
— 1 Chronicles 4:10
Because Jabez wasn’t praying from pride.

Not for ego—
but for purpose.

Not for control—
but for impact.
“That Your hand would be with me…”
Because he knew increase without God is destruction.
Because he didn’t trust himself with blessing without holiness.
This is where many of us miss it.

Pray small because of shame
or
Pray big because of pride
But Jabez shows a third way:
Bold prayers… with a surrendered heart.
Because the deeper issue isn’t territory.
You’re not just labeled by pain.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23
That’s the real name we carry.

And no amount of success, territory, or blessing
can erase that.
He didn’t just enlarge your territory.
Jesus took your sin, your shame, your failure, your past…

“He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.”
— 2 Corinthians 5:21

Jesus became what you were—
so you could become what He is.
You’re not begging as a rejected sinner.
You’re approaching as a redeemed child.

“Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace…”
— Hebrews 4:16
Why are you still praying like you’re disqualified?

Some of you are still shrinking your prayers
because you’re still believing old names.

Addict.
Failure.
Too late.
Too far gone.

“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
— 2 Corinthians 5:17

But this time—
don’t pray from shame.

“Lord, bless me—not so I can feel important,
but so I can serve Your purpose.”

“Enlarge my life—not for my name,
but for Your Kingdom.”

“Keep Your hand on me—
because I don’t trust myself without You.”

“Guard me from evil—
because I know what I’m capable of.”

“And anchor me in Jesus—
because He is my only righteousness.”
Are your prayers small because of shame?

That means turning—
from self-reliance, from sin, from silence—

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
You are not too far gone.

You are invited.
You are forgiven.
You are made new.
